correctness.rationale: For arbitrary characteristic-two fields and all n>=2, the Rota–Baxter identity forces P(1) to be a multiplicative idempotent, hence 0 or 1; the (1,b) identity forces P²=P. Idempotent weight-one maps are exactly projections onto complementary subalgebras. In a truncated one-generator local algebra, an element with nonzero t coefficient generates the maximal ideal through its powers. These claims exclude all but two splittings with P(1)=0; complements provide two more. All four converse cases satisfy the identity. Standalone exhaustive verification tests every linear map over seven finite-field/dimension combinations (including 262144 maps over F4 in dimension 3) and matches four operators exactly. Finite checks corroborate, but do not replace, the general proof.

value.rationale: The recent square-zero classification motivates a natural next problem: does extending a principal nilpotent thickening beyond first order create new operators? The complete theorem answers this for all lengths and every characteristic-two field: no new weight-one operators at any order, exactly four maps, rigid ranks and automorphism orbits. The reason is the one-dimensional cotangent space and its power-triangularity, not a finite-table coincidence. This is a natural all-length classification and exposes a structural boundary against multi-generator square-zero cases, where idempotent-matrix families are larger.
